bugs.what: Generic 'curio' trinket items silently changed name/description with no player action. 'a small worn ring' (found in Sunken Howe, Fenmarch) became 'a bog-glass bead necklace'; 'a cracked spyglass' (Flood-Watch tower) became 'a sergeant's brass whistle'; 'a hand-drawn charm against the gray' (given by Yarrow) became 'a woven eel-trap charm'; 'a broken hunting knife' (Eel-Run den) became 'a coil of tarred eel-line'. The swap happened somewhere between leaving Thornwold and arriving in the Iron Downs, confirmed stable across two consecutive status checks afterward. Contradicts state: the same carried objects should keep their identity.

Explicit route text was not enough to actually find the destination. Status said 'the Keepers' pilgrim stair at Coldpass opens for you now. North through Wardmoor, past Highward,' and from the ruined signal tower's top the text literally says 'Coldpass is a white line north.' Despite that, walking the full moor (Last Cairn, Oath-Ground, Long Sight, Windbreak Stones, Tower Rise/signal tower, Waystation Track, Drover's Rest, West Shieling, Twin Ruts, Peat Score, Boot-Track Hollow — a closed loop) never produced an exit toward Coldpass or Marrowgate. This is what ultimately cost the run its ending.

'Cracked Adit' (a boarded, condemned mine north of Cinderhall's head-frame) resolves the 'work the already-loosened corner' check with a one-line success and a few gold, then offers no further exit ('go in') or any other action — reads as a stub/dead end rather than a deliberate small reward.

Check-odds phrasing '(roll N+ on the die; +X skill)' states the raw d20 value needed, not the total against the DC — e.g. 'roll 7+; +2 wits' resolved as 'd20:6+2=8 vs DC 10 (10+ succeeds) — fail,' i.e. the die alone had to hit 8, not the total hit 7. Took several actual resolutions to confirm this reading; easy to misjudge your odds from the menu alone.

confusions: Never located the physical transition from Wardmoor to Coldpass/Marrowgate despite two independent, explicit textual pointers (quest log direction and a horizon sighting); the moor's rooms form a closed loop with no unexplored exit toward it that I could find.

No sense of how many turns a given hold or path will cost before committing to it — the opening screen warns the main road is ~300 turns and full completion 'many times that,' but nothing in status helps ration a fixed turn budget against that scope, so it's easy (as happened here) to spend the whole budget on 3 of 6 holds plus hub content and never reach the finale.
Renamed curio items (see bug above) made it briefly unclear whether a specific found object (e.g. the ring from the Howe) was still carried or had been replaced/lost.
suggestions: Once the Coldpass/pilgrim-stair condition unlocks, add it directly to the 'travel to a known place' list, or give one landmark (e.g. Highward's gate, or the Oath-Ground once resolved) an explicit 'go to Coldpass' option instead of requiring undirected cardinal-direction wandering to find it.

Keep picked-up curio/trinket names stable for the rest of the game, or if they're meant to be interchangeable flavor loot, label the slot generically ('assorted curios') so players don't mistake the rename for losing an item.
Give 'Cracked Adit' and similar one-off skill-check rooms a closing line ('nothing more to find here') so they don't read as unfinished content.
Surface a rough turn-cost estimate per hold/quest line in status (even a coarse 'short/medium/long') so players can budget a fixed turn count against the game's very large stated scope.
State check odds as the total needed against the shown DC (or show the DC directly) rather than the raw-die threshold, to match how players actually reason about their bonus.
